Jamie Parsons reports Erica missing.
Erica's remains found in Chesterfield, South Carolina.
Sandy and Casey Parsons convicted of murder.

name: Shannan Gilbert
summary: Sex worker Shannan Gilbert's disappearance at Oak Beach, Long Island led to the discovery of the Gilgo Beach serial killer's victims. Rex Heuermann was charged in 2023.
lastSeen: May 1, 2010, Oak Beach, Long Island, New York

sources.title: Shannan Gilbert - Wikipedia
Gilgo Beach murders - New York Times
Rex Heuermann arrest - NBC News

narrative: On May 1, 2010, twenty-four-year-old Shannan Gilbert, a sex worker from Jersey City, arrived at the Oak Beach community on Long Island's barrier island for an appointment arranged through Craigslist. During the encounter, she became distressed and fled the client's home, banging on neighbors' doors and making a frantic 911 call before running into the nearby marshland.

Shannan was never seen alive again. The search for her led police to make a shocking discovery: beginning in December 2010, investigators found the remains of multiple other victims along Ocean Parkway near Gilgo Beach, eventually uncovering at least 10 sets of human remains, revealing a serial killer had been operating on Long Island.

Shannan's body was found in the marsh near Oak Beach in December 2011. Her death was initially attributed to accidental drowning, though her family disputed this finding and believed she was a victim of the serial killer.

In July 2023, Rex Heuermann, a 59-year-old architect from Massapequa Park, was arrested and charged with multiple Gilgo Beach murders. As of 2024, he had been charged with the murders of several victims but not Shannan Gilbert. The investigation continues.

timeline.event: Shannan Gilbert disappears at Oak Beach.
Search for Shannan leads to discovery of Gilgo Beach victims.
Shannan's body found in a marsh near Oak Beach.
Rex Heuermann arrested for Gilgo Beach murders.

name: Lena Chapin
summary: Seventeen-year-old Lena Chapin vanished from rural Missouri. Her mother Sandy Klemp is suspected of involvement. Lena allegedly witnessed her mother kill her stepfather years earlier.
lastSeen: October 2006, Macks Creek, Camden County, Missouri

sources.title: Disappearance of Lena Chapin - Ozarks First
Lena Chapin case - 48 Hours CBS
Lena Chapin - Charley Project

narrative: In October 2006, seventeen-year-old Lena Marie Chapin disappeared from Macks Creek, a small community in Camden County, Missouri. Her mother, Sandra 'Sandy' Klemp, told family members that Lena had run away to be with a truck driver boyfriend, but no evidence of this relationship was ever found.

Years later, several of Lena's sisters came forward alleging that their mother had killed their stepfather Gary McCullough in 1999 and that Lena had been a witness. They believed Sandy killed Lena to prevent her from revealing what she had seen.

One sister produced a video in which Lena, at age 12, appeared to describe witnessing her mother kill Gary McCullough by hitting him with a vehicle. Gary's body was found in a burned truck, and his death was initially ruled accidental.

Despite the sisters' allegations and renewed investigation, Sandy Klemp has not been charged in connection with either Lena's disappearance or Gary's death. The case was featured on CBS's 48 Hours in 2018.

timeline.event: Lena Chapin vanishes from Macks Creek, Missouri.
Case featured on CBS 48 Hours; sisters allege mother's involvement.

name: Sandra Cantu
summary: Eight-year-old Sandra Cantu was murdered by Melissa Huckaby, a Sunday school teacher and neighbor in Tracy, California. Huckaby pleaded guilty to murder and kidnapping.
lastSeen: March 27, 2009, Orchard Estates Mobile Home Park, Tracy, California

sources.title: Murder of Sandra Cantu - Wikipedia
Melissa Huckaby case - San Francisco Chronicle
Sandra Cantu case - CNN

narrative: On March 27, 2009, eight-year-old Sandra Cantu went outside to play at the Orchard Estates Mobile Home Park in Tracy, California, and never returned. Surveillance cameras captured her walking in the mobile home park that afternoon, and a massive search was launched.
Ten days later, Sandra's body was found stuffed inside a suitcase in an irrigation pond near the mobile home park. She had been drugged, sexually assaulted, and asphyxiated.

Investigators traced the suitcase to Melissa Huckaby, 28, a Sunday school teacher who lived in the same mobile home park and whose daughter was Sandra's playmate. Huckaby, a granddaughter of a local pastor, had lured Sandra to her home.

Huckaby pleaded guilty to kidnapping and first-degree murder with a special circumstance of murder during kidnapping. She was sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole. The case was notable as female perpetrated child homicides of this nature are extremely rare.

timeline.event: Sandra Cantu disappears from her mobile home park in Tracy.
Sandra's body found in a suitcase in an irrigation pond.
Melissa Huckaby pleads guilty; sentenced to life without parole.

name: Ahmaud Arbery
summary: Ahmaud Arbery was chased and shot dead while jogging in Brunswick, Georgia by three white men. The case sparked national outrage over racial violence. All three were convicted of murder.
lastSeen: February 23, 2020, Satilla Shores neighborhood, Brunswick, Georgia

sources.title: Murder of Ahmaud Arbery - Wikipedia
Arbery trial verdict - New York Times
Ahmaud Arbery case - CNN

narrative: On February 23, 2020, twenty-five-year-old Ahmaud Marquez Arbery was jogging through the Satilla Shores neighborhood near Brunswick, Georgia, when he was pursued by three white men in pickup trucks. Gregory McMichael, his son Travis McMichael, and their neighbor William 'Roddie' Bryan Jr. chased Arbery for several minutes before Travis McMichael fatally shot him with a shotgun.

The McMichaels claimed they suspected Arbery of committing burglaries in the neighborhood and were attempting a citizen's arrest. Bryan filmed the confrontation on his cellphone. Despite the video evidence, no arrests were made for over two months, as local prosecutors initially declined to press charges.

The cellphone video was leaked in May 2020, sparking national outrage and protests. The Georgia Bureau of Investigation took over the case, and all three men were arrested and charged with murder. The case became part of a broader national reckoning about racial violence and the criminal justice system.

In November 2021, all three defendants were found guilty of murder in state court. Travis McMichael and his father received life sentences without parole; Bryan received life with the possibility of parole. All three were subsequently convicted of federal hate crimes in February 2022.

timeline.event: Ahmaud Arbery shot and killed while jogging in Brunswick, Georgia.
Cellphone video leaked; national outrage follows.
All three suspects arrested after GBI takes over investigation.
All three convicted of murder.

name: Kelsey Berreth
summary: Pilot and flight instructor Kelsey Berreth was murdered on Thanksgiving Day by her fiancé Patrick Frazee in Woodland Park, Colorado. He burned her body. Frazee was sentenced to life.
lastSeen: November 22, 2018, her townhome in Woodland Park, Colorado

sources.title: Murder of Kelsey Berreth - Wikipedia
Patrick Frazee trial - Denver Post
Kelsey Berreth case - CNN

narrative: On November 22, 2018, Thanksgiving Day, twenty-nine-year-old Kelsey Berreth, a pilot and flight instructor, was last seen on surveillance video entering a Woodland Park, Colorado Safeway store with her one-year-old daughter Kaylee. She was never seen again.

Kelsey's fiancé Patrick Frazee reported her missing on December 2 after her employer raised concerns. Text messages had been sent from Kelsey's phone for several days after her disappearance, leading investigators to initially believe she was alive. However, the texts had been sent by Frazee's girlfriend, Krystal Lee Kenney, at his direction.

Kenney became a key cooperating witness. She testified that Frazee had bludgeoned Kelsey to death with a baseball bat at her townhome and then enlisted Kenney to clean the crime scene and help dispose of the body, which was burned on Frazee's ranch. Kelsey's remains were never recovered.

Frazee was convicted of first-degree murder, solicitation of murder, and tampering with a body in November 2019. He was sentenced to life in prison without parole plus 156 years. Kenney pleaded guilty to tampering with evidence and was sentenced to three years.

timeline.event: Kelsey Berreth last seen alive on Thanksgiving Day.
Patrick Frazee arrested and charged with murder.
Frazee convicted of murder; sentenced to life without parole.

name: Dylan Redwine
summary: Thirteen-year-old Dylan Redwine disappeared during a court-ordered visit with his father Mark in Bayfield, Colorado. Mark Redwine was convicted of his murder in 2021.
lastSeen: November 19, 2012, his father's home near Bayfield, Colorado

sources.title: Murder of Dylan Redwine - Wikipedia
Mark Redwine trial - Durango Herald
Dylan Redwine case - NBC News

narrative: On November 19, 2012, thirteen-year-old Dylan Redwine traveled from his mother's home in Colorado Springs to his father Mark Redwine's home near Bayfield, Colorado, for a court-ordered Thanksgiving visit. Dylan and his father had a strained relationship. Mark reported Dylan missing the following day.

Despite extensive searches of the rugged terrain around Bayfield, Dylan was not found. In June 2013, hikers discovered some of Dylan's remains in a remote area about 10 miles from Mark's home. Additional remains, including Dylan's skull, were found in 2015.

The investigation focused on Mark Redwine, who had been the last person to see Dylan alive. Evidence revealed that Dylan had found disturbing photographs on his father's computer and had confronted him about them, providing a possible motive.
Mark Redwine was arrested in 2017 and charged with second-degree murder and child abuse. He was convicted in 2021 and sentenced to 48 years in prison.

timeline.event: Dylan Redwine arrives at his father's home; disappears overnight.
Some of Dylan's remains found in a remote area.
Mark Redwine arrested and charged with murder.
Mark Redwine convicted; sentenced to 48 years.

name: Heather Elvis
summary: Twenty-year-old Heather Elvis vanished from a boat landing in Myrtle Beach. The married couple she had been involved with, Sidney and Tammy Moorer, were convicted of kidnapping.
lastSeen: December 18, 2013, Peachtree Boat Landing, Myrtle Beach, South Carolina

sources.title: Disappearance of Heather Elvis - Wikipedia
Heather Elvis case - Myrtle Beach Sun News
Moorer trials - WMBF News

narrative: On December 18, 2013, twenty-year-old Heather Elvis left her apartment in Conway, South Carolina, in the early morning hours and drove to the Peachtree Boat Landing along the Intracoastal Waterway near Myrtle Beach. Her car was found at the boat landing with her personal belongings inside. Heather was never seen again.

The investigation revealed Heather had been having an affair with Sidney Moorer, a married man. When Sidney's wife Tammy discovered the affair, she confronted Heather and allegedly threatened her. Phone records showed Sidney called Heather shortly before she drove to the boat landing.

Sidney and Tammy Moorer were arrested and charged with kidnapping and murder. Phone records, GPS data, and surveillance footage placed them near the boat landing on the night Heather disappeared. Despite the evidence, prosecutors were unable to locate Heather's body.

Tammy Moorer was convicted of kidnapping and conspiracy in 2019 and sentenced to 30 years. Sidney Moorer was convicted of kidnapping in a separate trial. Without a body, the murder charges remain pending.

timeline.event: Heather Elvis vanishes from Peachtree Boat Landing.
Sidney and Tammy Moorer arrested.
Tammy Moorer convicted of kidnapping; sentenced to 30 years.

name: Alissa Turney
summary: Seventeen-year-old Alissa Turney disappeared from her Phoenix high school. Her stepfather Michael Turney was convicted of her murder in 2020 after her sister's advocacy campaign.
lastSeen: May 17, 2001, Paradise Valley High School, Phoenix, Arizona

sources.title: Disappearance of Alissa Turney - Wikipedia
Michael Turney conviction - AZ Central
Alissa Turney case - ABC15

narrative: On May 17, 2001, seventeen-year-old Alissa Turney disappeared from Paradise Valley High School in Phoenix, Arizona, on the last day of school. Her stepfather Michael Turney told police that Alissa had left a note saying she was running away to California, but the family was suspicious from the start.

The case went cold for years, despite Alissa's older sister Sarah Turney's persistent advocacy. Sarah launched a social media campaign and podcast called 'Voices for Justice' that brought renewed attention to the case and questioned Michael Turney's account.

The investigation intensified when Michael Turney was arrested in 2008 on an unrelated charge of attempting to blow up the offices of the Arizona Department of Economic Security. During the search of his home, investigators found extensive journals and evidence related to Alissa's disappearance.

In 2020, Michael Turney was arrested and charged with second-degree murder. He was convicted and sentenced to life in prison. Alissa's body has never been found. Sarah Turney's advocacy was credited as a key factor in bringing the case back to life.

timeline.event: Alissa Turney disappears from her Phoenix high school.
Michael Turney arrested on unrelated charges; evidence found.
Michael Turney convicted of second-degree murder; sentenced to life.

name: Jessica Chambers
summary: Nineteen-year-old Jessica Chambers was doused in a flammable liquid and set on fire in rural Mississippi. Quinton Tellis was tried twice; the second jury convicted him.
lastSeen: December 6, 2014, Courtland, Panola County, Mississippi

sources.title: Murder of Jessica Chambers - Wikipedia
Quinton Tellis trial - Clarion Ledger
Jessica Chambers case - CNN

narrative: On December 6, 2014, nineteen-year-old Jessica Chambers was found walking on a road near her burning car in Courtland, a small town in Panola County, Mississippi. She had been doused in a flammable liquid and set ablaze. She was airlifted to a Memphis hospital where she died from burns covering 98% of her body.

Before dying, Jessica reportedly tried to communicate the name of her attacker to first responders, but her injuries made it difficult to understand her. The case drew national attention due to its horrifying nature and the rural Mississippi setting.
In 2016, Quinton Tellis, a 27-year-old who had been linked to Jessica through phone records and witness statements, was charged with capital murder. His first trial in 2017 ended in a hung jury.

A second trial in 2018 also initially appeared headed for a mistrial, but the jury ultimately convicted Tellis of murder. He was sentenced to life in prison. The case highlighted the challenges of prosecuting violent crimes in small, rural communities.

timeline.event: Jessica Chambers found burning near her car in Courtland, Mississippi.
Jessica dies at a Memphis hospital from severe burns.
Quinton Tellis's first trial ends in hung jury.
Tellis convicted of murder; sentenced to life.

name: Brian Carrick
summary: Sixteen-year-old Brian Carrick disappeared after leaving his home in McHenry, Illinois. He was last seen at a gas station. Despite extensive searches, he has never been found.
lastSeen: October 18, 2002, McHenry, Illinois

sources.title: Brian Carrick case - Daily Herald
Brian Carrick - NCMEC
McHenry County cold cases

narrative: On October 18, 2002, sixteen-year-old Brian Joseph Carrick left his family's home in McHenry, Illinois, a suburban community northwest of Chicago. He was last seen at a gas station near his home. He never returned and has not been seen since.

Brian's family reported him missing when he failed to come home. An extensive search was conducted, but no trace of Brian was found. His case was investigated by the McHenry Police Department and the FBI.
Several persons of interest were identified over the years, but no charges were filed. The case has been periodically reviewed, and renewed appeals for information have been made.
Brian's family has remained active in keeping his case in the public eye. He is listed with the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children.

timeline.event: Brian Carrick leaves his McHenry home and vanishes.
Last seen at a gas station near his home.

name: Holly Branagan
summary: Fifteen-year-old Holly Branagan was stabbed to death in her Camp Hill, Pennsylvania home. In 2021, DNA evidence led to the arrest of Joseph Haines, a former classmate.
lastSeen: March 30, 1979, her home in Camp Hill, Pennsylvania

sources.title: Murder of Holly Branagan - PennLive
Joseph Haines arrested - ABC27
Holly Branagan case - Cumberland County DA

narrative: On March 30, 1979, fifteen-year-old Holly Branagan was found stabbed to death in the living room of her family's home in Camp Hill, Pennsylvania, a suburb of Harrisburg. She had been home alone after school when someone entered the house and attacked her.
The investigation was extensive but yielded no arrests. Forensic evidence including blood and fingerprints was collected at the scene, but technology at the time could not identify the killer.
For over 40 years, the case remained one of Cumberland County's most prominent cold cases. Holly's family never gave up hope that advances in forensic technology would identify her killer.

In 2021, genetic genealogy analysis of DNA evidence from the crime scene identified Joseph Haines, a former classmate of Holly's who had attended Cedar Cliff High School with her. Haines was arrested, and his DNA was confirmed to match the evidence. He was charged with first-degree murder.

timeline.event: Holly Branagan found stabbed to death in her Camp Hill home.
Joseph Haines arrested through DNA and genetic genealogy.

name: Sierah Joughin
summary: Twenty-year-old Sierah Joughin was abducted while bicycling in rural Ohio. James Worley, a convicted kidnapper, was convicted of her murder and sentenced to death.
lastSeen: July 19, 2016, County Road 6, Metamora, Fulton County, Ohio

sources.title: Murder of Sierah Joughin - Wikipedia
James Worley conviction - Toledo Blade
Sierah's Law - Ohio Legislature

narrative: On July 19, 2016, twenty-year-old Sierah Joughin went for a bicycle ride with her boyfriend near her home in rural Fulton County, Ohio. When her boyfriend turned back, Sierah continued riding alone. She never returned.

Sierah's bicycle was found on the road near the farm of James Daniel Worley, a 57-year-old with a 1990 conviction for abducting a woman on a bicycle in the same area. Investigators searched Worley's property and found Sierah's body buried in a shallow grave on his land.
Worley was arrested and charged with aggravated murder and kidnapping. Evidence included motorcycle parts matching a vehicle seen near the abduction site and traces of Sierah's DNA in Worley's home.

Worley was convicted and sentenced to death in 2017. The case led to the passage of 'Sierah's Law' in Ohio, which created a publicly searchable database of violent offenders, expanding beyond the sex offender registry to include other violent criminals.

timeline.event: Sierah Joughin abducted while bicycling in rural Fulton County.
Sierah's body found buried on James Worley's property.
Worley convicted; sentenced to death.
'Sierah's Law' signed, creating violent offender database.

name: Gabby Petito
summary: Travel vlogger Gabby Petito was murdered by her fiancé Brian Laundrie during a cross-country road trip. Her body was found in Wyoming. Laundrie died by suicide in Florida.
lastSeen: August 27, 2021, Spread Creek Dispersed Camping Area, Bridger-Teton National Forest, Wyoming

sources.title: Murder of Gabby Petito - Wikipedia
Gabby Petito case - CNN
Brian Laundrie notebook - FBI

narrative: On September 11, 2021, the family of twenty-two-year-old Gabrielle 'Gabby' Petito reported her missing after she failed to respond to calls and texts during a cross-country road trip with her fiancé Brian Laundrie. The couple had been documenting their journey on social media and YouTube.

Laundrie had returned to his parents' home in North Port, Florida on September 1, driving Gabby's van alone, and refused to speak with police. Body camera footage from Moab, Utah police showed that officers had responded to a domestic disturbance involving the couple on August 12.

On September 19, Gabby's remains were found at the Spread Creek Dispersed Camping Area in Bridger-Teton National Forest in Wyoming. The coroner determined she had been strangled. The case generated unprecedented social media attention and public involvement.

Laundrie disappeared from his Florida home on September 13, sparking a massive manhunt. His skeletal remains were found in the Carlton Reserve in Sarasota County, Florida on October 20, along with a notebook in which he confessed to killing Gabby. He had died of a self-inflicted gunshot wound.

timeline.event: Moab police respond to domestic disturbance between Gabby and Brian.
Brian Laundrie returns to Florida alone in Gabby's van.
Gabby's remains found in Bridger-Teton National Forest.
Brian Laundrie's remains found with confession notebook.

name: Mary Agnes Moroney
summary: Mary Agnes Moroney, a Boston nurse, was found strangled in her Beacon Hill apartment. The case became one of Boston's most notorious unsolved murders of the early 20th century.
lastSeen: February 24, 1930, her apartment on Joy Street, Beacon Hill, Boston

sources.title: Boston cold cases - Boston Globe
Beacon Hill mysteries - New England Historical Society
Boston Police Department cold cases

narrative: On February 24, 1930, Mary Agnes Moroney, a 36-year-old nurse, was found strangled in her apartment on Joy Street in Boston's Beacon Hill neighborhood. There were no signs of forced entry, suggesting she may have known her killer.

The investigation was complicated by the social dynamics of 1930s Boston. Moroney lived alone and was described as a private person. Police interviewed numerous acquaintances and neighbors but were unable to identify a suspect.

The case received extensive coverage in Boston newspapers at the time, with various theories proposed about her killer. Some investigators believed the murder was related to a personal relationship, while others explored the possibility of a stranger attack.
Despite periodic reviews over the decades, the murder of Mary Agnes Moroney has never been solved. It remains one of Boston's oldest unsolved homicides.

timeline.event: Mary Agnes Moroney found strangled in her Beacon Hill apartment.
Boston police launch investigation; no suspects identified.

name: DeOrr Kunz Jr.
summary: Two-year-old DeOrr Kunz Jr. vanished from a campsite in the mountains near Leadore, Idaho. Despite extensive searches, he has never been found. His parents are considered persons of interest.
lastSeen: July 10, 2015, Timber Creek Campground, Lemhi County, Idaho

sources.title: Disappearance of DeOrr Kunz Jr. - Wikipedia
DeOrr Kunz case - East Idaho News
Lemhi County Sheriff investigation

narrative: On July 10, 2015, two-year-old DeOrr Jay Kunz Jr. vanished from the Timber Creek Campground in the mountains of Lemhi County, Idaho, while on a camping trip with his parents, his grandfather, and the grandfather's friend. His father, DeOrr Kunz Sr., reported the boy missing, saying he had looked away for a few minutes.

An intensive search of the rugged mountain terrain was launched, involving search and rescue teams, cadaver dogs, divers, and aircraft. The campground sits at approximately 7,000 feet elevation and is surrounded by dense forest. Despite extensive efforts, no trace of the toddler was found.

The investigation by the Lemhi County Sheriff's Office and FBI raised questions about the parents' account of events. Both parents failed polygraph examinations, and their stories contained inconsistencies. Private investigators hired by the family also expressed doubts about the parents' account.

DeOrr Kunz Sr. and the boy's mother, Jessica Mitchell, have been named as persons of interest but have not been charged. The absence of any physical evidence—no clothing, tracks, or remains—in such a remote and harsh environment has baffled investigators.

timeline.event: DeOrr Kunz Jr. reported missing from Timber Creek Campground.
Extensive search of mountain terrain finds no trace.
Parents named as persons of interest.

name: Jason Derek Brown
summary: Jason Derek Brown is wanted by the FBI for the murder and robbery of an armored car guard outside a movie theater in Phoenix, Arizona. He is believed to have fled to international destinations.
lastSeen: November 29, 2004, Ahwatukee, Phoenix, Arizona

sources.title: Jason Derek Brown - FBI Most Wanted
Jason Brown case - AZ Central
America's Most Wanted - Jason Brown

narrative: On November 29, 2004, an armored car guard named Robert Keith Palomares was shot and killed outside an AMC movie theater in the Ahwatukee neighborhood of Phoenix, Arizona. The gunman grabbed a bag of cash and fled the scene on a bicycle.

The investigation identified Jason Derek Brown, a 34-year-old businessman and avid golfer, as the prime suspect. Brown was known for his flashy lifestyle, driving luxury cars and frequenting expensive restaurants, despite being deeply in debt.

Brown vanished before he could be arrested. He was placed on the FBI's Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list in 2007. Investigators believe he may have fled to countries in Central America or to France, where he had traveled frequently.
As of 2024, Brown remains one of the longest-tenured names on the FBI's Most Wanted list. The FBI has offered a reward of up to $200,000 for information leading to his capture.

timeline.event: Robert Palomares murdered during armored car robbery in Phoenix.
Jason Derek Brown placed on FBI's Ten Most Wanted list.

name: Robert William Fisher
summary: Robert Fisher is wanted for killing his wife and two children and blowing up their Scottsdale home to cover the crime. He has been a fugitive since 2001.
lastSeen: April 10, 2001, near Payson, Arizona

sources.title: Robert Fisher - FBI Most Wanted
Robert Fisher case - Arizona Republic
Fisher family murders - CBS News

narrative: On April 10, 2001, an explosion and fire destroyed a home in Scottsdale, Arizona. Inside the wreckage, firefighters found the bodies of Mary Fisher, 38, and the couple's two children, Brittney, 12, and Bobby Jr., 10. All three had their throats slashed before the house was set ablaze.

The investigation quickly focused on Robert William Fisher, the husband and father, who was nowhere to be found. His SUV was discovered abandoned several days later near Payson, Arizona, at a trailhead leading into the rugged Tonto National Forest.

Fisher, a former firefighter and avid outdoorsman, was placed on the FBI's Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list in 2002. Investigators believe his knowledge of wilderness survival could enable him to live off the grid for extended periods.

Despite numerous reported sightings across the United States and internationally over more than two decades, Fisher has never been apprehended. The case remains one of the FBI's most prominent open investigations.

timeline.event: Fisher family home explodes; wife and children found murdered.
Fisher's SUV found abandoned near Payson.
Robert Fisher placed on FBI's Ten Most Wanted list.

name: Rui Pedro
summary: Eleven-year-old Rui Pedro Teixeira Mendonça disappeared from Lousada, Portugal. The case became one of Portugal's most high-profile child disappearances and sparked reforms in child protection.
lastSeen: March 4, 1998, Lousada, Porto District, Portugal

sources.title: Disappearance of Rui Pedro - Wikipedia
Rui Pedro case - Público
Rui Pedro - Polícia Judiciária

narrative: On March 4, 1998, eleven-year-old Rui Pedro Teixeira Mendonça disappeared from the town of Lousada in northern Portugal. The boy had been last seen in the company of a known local man, Afonso Dias, who was later convicted of kidnapping.

The investigation revealed deeply disturbing connections to a pedophilia network. A photograph allegedly showing Rui Pedro was found during an Interpol operation targeting child exploitation websites, but the identification was never conclusively confirmed.

Afonso Dias was convicted of kidnapping Rui Pedro and sentenced to 16 years in prison, but he never revealed the boy's whereabouts. The case became a national sensation in Portugal and exposed failures in the child protection system.
The case of Rui Pedro remains one of Portugal's most painful unsolved mysteries. It contributed to significant reforms in how Portugal handles missing children cases and child protection legislation.

timeline.event: Rui Pedro disappears from Lousada, Portugal.
Afonso Dias convicted of kidnapping.

name: Arlis Perry
summary: Newlywed Arlis Perry was murdered in Stanford Memorial Church in a ritualistic manner. The case went unsolved for 44 years until DNA linked security guard Stephen Crawford to the crime.
lastSeen: October 12, 1974, Stanford Memorial Church, Stanford, California

sources.title: Murder of Arlis Perry - Wikipedia
Arlis Perry case solved - Mercury News
Stanford church murder - San Francisco Chronicle

narrative: On October 12, 1974, nineteen-year-old Arlis Perry, a newlywed from Bismarck, North Dakota, was found murdered inside Stanford Memorial Church on the Stanford University campus in California. She had gone to the church to pray after an argument with her husband Bruce.

The crime scene was staged in a ritualistic manner that shocked investigators. Arlis had been strangled and stabbed, and religious objects were arranged around her body. The grotesque staging led to speculation about satanic involvement.

The case went cold for decades. Investigators periodically revisited the evidence but were unable to identify a suspect. The ritualistic nature of the crime generated extensive media coverage and true crime interest.

In 2018, genetic genealogy matched DNA from the crime scene to Stephen Blake Crawford, a former Stanford security guard who had been on duty the night of the murder. When investigators arrived at Crawford's home to arrest him, he died by suicide. The case was officially closed.

timeline.event: Arlis Perry murdered inside Stanford Memorial Church.
DNA identifies Stephen Crawford; he dies by suicide during arrest attempt.

name: Princess Doe
summary: An unidentified teenage girl was found bludgeoned to death in a Blairstown, New Jersey cemetery. Known as 'Princess Doe,' she has never been identified despite decades of investigation.
lastSeen: Found July 15, 1982, Cedar Ridge Cemetery, Blairstown, New Jersey

sources.title: Princess Doe - Wikipedia
Princess Doe case - NamUs
Princess Doe - Doe Network

narrative: On July 15, 1982, the body of an unidentified teenage girl was found in Cedar Ridge Cemetery in Blairstown, New Jersey. She had been bludgeoned to death with a rock and her face was severely disfigured, making visual identification impossible.

The girl, estimated to be between 14 and 18 years old, was given the name 'Princess Doe' by investigators. Despite widespread publicity and comparison to missing persons databases, she has never been identified.

In 1983, a man named Arthur Kinlaw was indicted for her murder based on witness testimony, but the charges were later dropped due to insufficient evidence. The identity of Princess Doe and her killer remain unknown.

The case was one of the earliest to be entered into the National Missing and Unidentified Persons System (NamUs). DNA profiles and isotope analysis have been conducted, but no match has been found. Princess Doe has become a symbol for all unidentified crime victims.

timeline.event: Unidentified girl found murdered in Blairstown, New Jersey cemetery.
Arthur Kinlaw indicted but charges later dropped.

name: Boy in the Box (Joseph Augustus Zarelli)
summary: A young boy's body found in a box in Philadelphia in 1957 went unidentified for 65 years. In 2022, DNA genealogy identified him as Joseph Augustus Zarelli.
lastSeen: Found February 25, 1957, Fox Chase area, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

sources.title: Boy in the Box - Wikipedia
Boy in the Box identified - Philadelphia Inquirer
Joseph Zarelli identification - AP News

narrative: On February 25, 1957, a boy's battered body was found wrapped in a plaid blanket inside a cardboard box in the Fox Chase area of Philadelphia. He appeared to be about 4 to 6 years old, malnourished, with recent haircut marks. He had been beaten to death.

Despite one of Philadelphia's most extensive investigations, the boy could not be identified. His fingerprints were taken and his photo was distributed on thousands of flyers placed in gas company bills across the region. He became known as 'America's Unknown Child.'

The case became one of the most famous unidentified person cases in American history. Multiple theories emerged over the decades. The boy was buried in a potter's field and later reinterred at Ivy Hill Cemetery under the name 'America's Unknown Child.'

In December 2022, genetic genealogy finally identified the boy as Joseph Augustus Zarelli. The identification came 65 years after his death. While his identity was established, no one has been charged with his murder, as the likely suspects have all died.

timeline.event: Body of unidentified boy found in a box in Philadelphia.
Body exhumed for DNA testing.
Identified as Joseph Augustus Zarelli through genetic genealogy.

name: El Dorado Jane Doe (Mercedes Cuevas)
summary: A woman found dead in an El Dorado, Arkansas motel in 1991 went unidentified for nearly 30 years. DNA genealogy identified her as Mercedes Cuevas from Guatemala in 2022.
lastSeen: Found April 14, 1991, Whitehall Motel, El Dorado, Arkansas

sources.title: El Dorado Jane Doe identified - DNA Doe Project
Mercedes Cuevas identification - Arkansas Democrat-Gazette
NamUs case

narrative: On April 14, 1991, a young woman was found dead in a room at the Whitehall Motel in El Dorado, Arkansas. She had no identification, and the cause of death was unclear. She was estimated to be in her late teens to early twenties.

For nearly three decades, investigators tried to identify the woman. Her case was entered into NamUs and featured on various missing persons databases. Multiple reconstructions were created, but no match was found in U.S. missing persons records.
The DNA Doe Project, a nonprofit using genetic genealogy to identify unidentified remains, took on the case. Through extensive genealogical research, they traced her family tree to Guatemala.
In 2022, the woman was identified as Mercedes Cuevas, who had emigrated from Guatemala to the United States. The identification brought answers to a case that had been open for over 30 years.

timeline.event: Unidentified woman found dead in El Dorado, Arkansas motel.
DNA genealogy identifies her as Mercedes Cuevas from Guatemala.

name: Belle in the Boot
summary: A woman's remains were found in a sleeping bag near a freeway in Pacific Palisades, California. She was wearing expensive Western boots. Her identity remains unknown.
lastSeen: Found November 1, 1996, along Pacific Coast Highway, Pacific Palisades, California

sources.title: Belle in the Boot - Doe Network
Belle in the Boot - NamUs
Belle in the Boot case - LAPD

narrative: On November 1, 1996, a woman's decomposed remains were found in a sleeping bag alongside the Pacific Coast Highway in Pacific Palisades, Los Angeles, California. The body had been there for an estimated two to four weeks.

The woman was wearing distinctive, expensive Tony Lama Western boots, which led investigators and the public to dub her 'Belle in the Boot.' She was estimated to be between 25 and 45 years old, approximately 5'4" tall, with brown hair.

Despite extensive investigation by the LAPD, comparison with missing persons databases, facial reconstruction, and DNA profiling, the woman has never been identified. Isotope analysis suggested she may have spent time in the southeastern United States.
The case remains one of Los Angeles's most puzzling unidentified person cases. She is listed in NamUs and the Doe Network.

timeline.event: Woman's remains found in a sleeping bag along Pacific Coast Highway.

name: Elijah Lewis
summary: Five-year-old Elijah Lewis was murdered and buried by his mother and her boyfriend in New Hampshire. His remains were found in Abington, Massachusetts. Both were convicted.
lastSeen: October 2020, Merrimack, New Hampshire

sources.title: Murder of Elijah Lewis - Wikipedia
Elijah Lewis case - WMUR
NH AG press release

narrative: In October 2021, authorities in New Hampshire launched a search for five-year-old Elijah Lewis after the state's Division for Children, Youth and Families reported the boy missing. His mother, Danielle Dauphinais, and her boyfriend, Joseph Stapf, had been telling people that Elijah was staying with friends.

Elijah's remains were found buried in a wooded area in Abington, Massachusetts, about 80 miles from the family's Merrimack, New Hampshire home. He had suffered extreme abuse and neglect before his death.

Both Dauphinais and Stapf were arrested and charged with murder. The investigation revealed a pattern of severe abuse, including malnutrition and physical violence, that Elijah had endured before his death around October 2020.

Dauphinais was convicted of second-degree murder and sentenced to 45 years to life. Stapf pleaded guilty to second-degree murder and was sentenced to 30 years to life. The case led to calls for reform of New Hampshire's child welfare system.

timeline.event: Elijah Lewis believed to have died (approximate date).
DCYF reports Elijah missing; investigation launched.
Elijah's remains found buried in Abington, Massachusetts.
Danielle Dauphinais convicted; sentenced to 45 years to life.

name: Orange Socks
summary: A woman wearing only orange socks was found murdered along I-35 in Texas in 1979. Serial killer Henry Lee Lucas confessed but his conviction was commuted. She remains unidentified.
lastSeen: Found October 31, 1979, Interstate 35, Georgetown, Texas

sources.title: Orange Socks - Wikipedia
Orange Socks - NamUs
Henry Lee Lucas - Texas Monthly

narrative: On Halloween 1979, the body of an unidentified woman was found in a culvert along Interstate 35 near Georgetown, Texas. She had been sexually assaulted and strangled. The only item of clothing on her body was a pair of orange socks, which became her identifier.

The case took a controversial turn in 1983 when serial killer Henry Lee Lucas confessed to the murder. Lucas, who was known for making hundreds of false confessions, was convicted and sentenced to death. However, evidence later suggested Lucas was in Florida at the time of the murder.

In 1998, Texas Governor George W. Bush commuted Lucas's death sentence to life imprisonment, the only such commutation during his tenure. Lucas died in prison in 2001. The murder conviction was widely questioned.
Despite advanced forensic testing including DNA analysis and isotope studies, the woman known as Orange Socks has never been identified. She remains one of Texas's most well-known Doe cases.

timeline.event: Unidentified woman found murdered along I-35 near Georgetown, Texas.
Henry Lee Lucas confesses; later convicted.
Governor Bush commutes Lucas's death sentence.

name: Cheryl Grimmer
summary: Three-year-old Cheryl Grimmer was snatched from the changing rooms of a beach shower block in Wollongong, Australia. A suspect was identified in 2017 but charges were dismissed.
lastSeen: January 12, 1970, Fairy Meadow Beach, Wollongong, New South Wales, Australia

sources.title: Disappearance of Cheryl Grimmer - Wikipedia
Cheryl Grimmer case - Sydney Morning Herald
NSW Police cold case review

narrative: On January 12, 1970, the Grimmer family, recent British immigrants to Australia, visited Fairy Meadow Beach near Wollongong, New South Wales. Three-year-old Cheryl went into a shower and changing block with her three older brothers. When the boys came out, Cheryl was gone.
A witness reportedly saw a man carrying a small child from the area, but the description was vague. Despite an immediate search and widespread publicity, Cheryl was never found.

The case lay dormant for decades until renewed investigation in the 2010s. In 2017, a man was arrested and charged with Cheryl's murder based on a witness statement from the 1970s. However, the charges were dismissed when the court ruled that the suspect's interview as a teenager in 1971 was inadmissible.
Cheryl Grimmer's disappearance remains one of Australia's most enduring cold cases. Her family, including her brothers who were present at the time, have continued to seek answers.

timeline.event: Cheryl Grimmer snatched from a beach shower block in Wollongong.
Suspect arrested but charges later dismissed.

name: Haleigh Cummings
summary: Five-year-old Haleigh Cummings vanished from her father's mobile home in Satsuma, Florida. Her father's girlfriend Misty Croslin was babysitting. No one has been charged.
lastSeen: February 9, 2009, her father's mobile home, Satsuma, Florida

sources.title: Disappearance of Haleigh Cummings - Wikipedia
Haleigh Cummings case - Florida Times-Union
Putnam County Sheriff investigation

narrative: On February 9, 2009, five-year-old Haleigh Cummings was reported missing from her father Ronald Cummings's mobile home in Satsuma, a rural community in Putnam County, Florida. Ronald's 17-year-old girlfriend, Misty Croslin, was babysitting Haleigh and her younger brother when she said she woke up and found Haleigh gone.

Misty told police she had put Haleigh to bed and then gone to sleep herself. When she woke up around 3 a.m., the back door was propped open and Haleigh was missing. Her account contained inconsistencies that changed over time.

The investigation was hampered by the chaotic personal lives of those involved. Ronald Cummings and Misty Croslin married shortly after the disappearance but later divorced. Both were subsequently arrested on drug trafficking charges unrelated to Haleigh's case.
Despite extensive searches of the surrounding area, including the St. Johns River, Haleigh has never been found. The Putnam County Sheriff's Office continues to investigate.

timeline.event: Haleigh Cummings reported missing from Satsuma, Florida.
Ronald Cummings and Misty Croslin arrested on drug charges.

name: Elsie Paroubek
summary: Five-year-old Elsie Paroubek vanished from her Chicago neighborhood in 1911. Her body was found in a drainage canal weeks later. The case inspired one of outsider artist Henry Darger's works.
lastSeen: April 8, 1911, near her home in Chicago, Illinois

sources.title: Disappearance of Elsie Paroubek - Wikipedia
Elsie Paroubek and Henry Darger - Chicago Magazine
Elsie Paroubek - Chicago Tribune archives

narrative: On April 8, 1911, five-year-old Elsie Paroubek, the daughter of Czech immigrants, vanished from the area near her family's home in Chicago's Pilsen neighborhood. She had been playing with her cousin when she disappeared.

A massive search was launched, and the case became front-page news across Chicago. Rewards were offered, and thousands of people participated in the search. The case highlighted the vulnerability of children in the rapidly growing industrial city.

On May 8, exactly one month after her disappearance, Elsie's body was found in a drainage canal on the outskirts of Chicago. The cause of death was drowning, but the circumstances remained unclear. No one was ever charged.

Elsie's case had an unexpected cultural legacy. Outsider artist Henry Darger, who lived in Chicago, was deeply affected by the newspaper coverage of her disappearance. He incorporated her image into his monumental work 'In the Realms of the Unreal.'

timeline.event: Elsie Paroubek vanishes from her Chicago neighborhood.
Elsie's body found in a drainage canal.

name: Ben Needham
summary: Twenty-one-month-old Ben Needham vanished from outside his grandparents' farmhouse on the Greek island of Kos. Despite decades of investigation, he has never been found.
lastSeen: July 24, 1991, outside grandparents' farmhouse, Iraklis, Kos, Greece

sources.title: Disappearance of Ben Needham - Wikipedia
Ben Needham case - BBC
Kerry Needham campaign - ITV

narrative: On July 24, 1991, twenty-one-month-old Ben Needham was playing outside his grandparents' farmhouse in Iraklis, a small village on the Greek island of Kos. His mother Kerry had traveled from Sheffield, England, with Ben to visit her parents, who were renovating a farmhouse on the island. Ben vanished while his mother was inside.

Initial theories focused on abduction, with suggestions that Ben may have been taken by a childless couple. Greek and British police conducted extensive searches and interviews on Kos. The investigation was hampered by language barriers and jurisdictional complications.

In 2012, South Yorkshire Police took a more active role in the investigation. New forensic work was conducted at the farmhouse site. In 2016, police explored the theory that a construction worker at the property may have accidentally killed Ben with a digger and buried the evidence. The worker, Konstantinos Barkas, had died before he could be questioned.
Ben's mother Kerry has campaigned for over three decades to find her son. The case remains the subject of periodic police operations, but Ben has never been found.

timeline.event: Ben Needham vanishes from the village of Iraklis on Kos.
Police investigate theory of accidental death at construction site.

name: Lauren Spierer
summary: Indiana University student Lauren Spierer vanished after a night out in Bloomington, Indiana. Despite massive searches and national attention, she has never been found.
lastSeen: June 3, 2011, walking near 11th Street, Bloomington, Indiana

sources.title: Disappearance of Lauren Spierer - Wikipedia
Lauren Spierer case - Indianapolis Star
FindLauren.com

narrative: In the early morning hours of June 3, 2011, twenty-year-old Lauren Spierer, a sophomore at Indiana University, was last seen walking alone near her apartment complex in Bloomington, Indiana, after a night of drinking at several bars and a party.

Surveillance footage and witness accounts pieced together Lauren's movements through the night. She was seen leaving Kilroy's Sports Bar, visiting a friend's apartment, and then walking toward her own apartment without shoes and without her phone or keys. She was last seen at approximately 4:30 a.m.

A massive search involving thousands of volunteers combed Bloomington and the surrounding areas. Several male friends who were with Lauren that night were questioned but retained lawyers and declined to cooperate fully with the investigation.
Lauren Spierer has never been found. Her parents, Robert and Charlene Spierer, have maintained a public campaign through FindLauren.com.

timeline.event: Lauren Spierer last seen walking near her Bloomington apartment.

name: Laci Peterson
summary: Pregnant Laci Peterson vanished from her Modesto, California home on Christmas Eve. Her husband Scott Peterson was convicted of double murder and sentenced to death, later commuted to life.
lastSeen: December 24, 2002, her home on Covena Avenue, Modesto, California

sources.title: Murder of Laci Peterson - Wikipedia
Scott Peterson trial - CNN
Laci Peterson case - Modesto Bee

narrative: On December 24, 2002, Laci Denise Peterson, 27 and eight months pregnant, was reported missing by her husband Scott from their home in Modesto, California. Scott claimed he had gone fishing at the Berkeley Marina that morning and returned to find Laci gone.

The investigation quickly focused on Scott Peterson. He had been having an affair with massage therapist Amber Frey, who cooperated with police and secretly recorded their phone calls. Scott displayed behavior that investigators found suspicious, including selling Laci's car and exploring options for selling their home.

In April 2003, the bodies of Laci and her unborn son Conner washed ashore in San Francisco Bay, near where Scott said he had been fishing. Scott was arrested while apparently attempting to flee to Mexico.

Scott Peterson was convicted of first-degree murder of Laci and second-degree murder of Conner in 2004, and sentenced to death. His death sentence was overturned in 2020 on procedural grounds and he was resentenced to life without parole in 2021.

timeline.event: Laci Peterson reported missing from her Modesto home.
Laci and Conner's remains found in San Francisco Bay.
Scott Peterson convicted of double murder.

name: Lacey Fletcher
summary: Lacey Fletcher was found dead in deplorable conditions on a couch in her parents' home in Slaughter, Louisiana. She had been neglected for at least 12 years. Both parents were charged with murder.
lastSeen: January 3, 2022, found deceased in her parents' home, Slaughter, Louisiana

sources.title: Death of Lacey Fletcher - Wikipedia
Lacey Fletcher case - The Advocate
Fletcher parents charged - NBC News

narrative: On January 3, 2022, first responders in Slaughter, Louisiana were called to the home of Clay and Sheila Fletcher, who reported that their 36-year-old daughter Lacey had died. What responders found was described as one of the most horrific scenes they had ever encountered.

Lacey Fletcher was found dead, fused to a couch in the living room. The coroner determined she had been sitting in the same spot for at least 12 years, developing severe pressure ulcers, malnutrition, and bone infections. She weighed only 96 pounds and had been living in her own waste.

Lacey had been diagnosed with autism and social anxiety as a child. Rather than seeking appropriate care, her parents had allowed her to deteriorate on the couch while they lived in the same house. Neighbors and officials had reportedly not checked on Lacey for years.

Both Clay and Sheila Fletcher were charged with second-degree murder. The case raised serious questions about the oversight of disabled adults and the failure of community systems to identify severe neglect.

timeline.event: Lacey Fletcher found dead in her parents' home.
Clay and Sheila Fletcher charged with second-degree murder.

name: Carol Stuart
summary: Charles Stuart murdered his pregnant wife Carol and blamed a Black carjacker, triggering a racist manhunt in Boston. Stuart jumped to his death when the truth emerged.
lastSeen: October 23, 1989, Mission Hill, Boston, Massachusetts

sources.title: Murder of Carol Stuart - Wikipedia
Stuart case - Boston Globe
Charles Stuart case - New York Times

narrative: On October 23, 1989, Charles Stuart called 911 from his car in the Mission Hill neighborhood of Boston, claiming he and his pregnant wife Carol had been shot by a Black carjacker. Carol, seven months pregnant, died from a gunshot wound to the head. Their baby, Christopher, was delivered by emergency cesarean but died 17 days later.

The case inflamed racial tensions in Boston. Police conducted aggressive stop-and-frisk operations in Mission Hill, a predominantly Black neighborhood. William Bennett, a Black man, was identified by Charles Stuart in a lineup and was about to be charged.

The truth emerged in January 1990 when Charles's brother Matthew went to police and revealed that Charles had shot Carol himself, likely for insurance money. Matthew had disposed of the gun and Carol's jewelry.

On January 4, 1990, the day after his brother's confession, Charles Stuart jumped to his death from the Tobin Bridge into the Mystic River. The case became a searing example of racial bias in the criminal justice system and a defining moment in Boston's history of racial tension.

timeline.event: Carol Stuart shot and killed; Charles blames a Black carjacker.
Matthew Stuart reveals Charles killed Carol.
Charles Stuart dies by suicide.

name: Dorothea Puente Victims
summary: Landlady Dorothea Puente murdered her elderly and disabled tenants in Sacramento, burying them in her garden while continuing to collect their Social Security checks.
lastSeen: Various dates, 1426 F Street, Sacramento, California

sources.title: Dorothea Puente - Wikipedia
Puente case - Sacramento Bee
Puente murders - History Channel

narrative: Dorothea Puente operated a boarding house at 1426 F Street in Sacramento, California, where she rented rooms to elderly, disabled, and mentally ill tenants. Between 1982 and 1988, she murdered at least seven of her tenants, burying their bodies in her yard while continuing to cash their Social Security and disability checks.

The murders came to light on November 11, 1988, when police investigating a missing tenant began digging in Puente's garden. They found one body, then another, and eventually uncovered seven sets of remains buried in the small yard.
Puente was arrested while attempting to flee to Mexico. She maintained her innocence, claiming her tenants had died of natural causes and she had simply buried them because she panicked.

She was convicted of three counts of first-degree murder in 1993 and sentenced to life in prison without parole. She died in prison in 2011 at age 82. Her former boarding house has become a macabre tourist attraction.

timeline.event: First body discovered in Puente's garden.
Seven bodies total found; Puente arrested.
Puente convicted of three murders; sentenced to life.

name: Kathleen Peterson
summary: Kathleen Peterson was found dead at the bottom of a staircase. Her husband Michael claimed she fell. He was convicted of murder, the subject of 'The Staircase' documentary.
lastSeen: December 9, 2001, her home on Cedar Street, Durham, North Carolina

sources.title: Death of Kathleen Peterson - Wikipedia
The Staircase documentary - Netflix
Michael Peterson trial - WRAL

narrative: On December 9, 2001, novelist Michael Peterson called 911 to report that his wife Kathleen, 48, had fallen down the stairs at their Durham, North Carolina home and was unconscious. Paramedics found Kathleen dead at the bottom of the staircase in a massive pool of blood.

The medical examiner determined that Kathleen's injuries were inconsistent with a fall, noting deep lacerations on her scalp and blood spatter patterns suggesting a beating. Michael Peterson was charged with first-degree murder.

The case was complicated by the discovery that a family friend in Germany, Elizabeth Ratliff, had also been found dead at the bottom of a staircase in 1985 when Peterson was living nearby. Ratliff's death was subsequently reclassified as a homicide.

Peterson was convicted of first-degree murder in 2003. He received a new trial in 2011 after it was found that a key prosecution blood analyst had given misleading testimony. In 2017, Peterson entered an Alford plea to voluntary manslaughter and was sentenced to time served. The case was the subject of the acclaimed documentary 'The Staircase.'

timeline.event: Kathleen Peterson found dead at the bottom of a staircase.
Michael Peterson convicted of first-degree murder.
Peterson enters Alford plea to manslaughter; sentenced to time served.

name: Holly Maddux
summary: Holly Maddux was murdered by Ira Einhorn, a prominent counterculture figure in Philadelphia. Her body was found in a trunk in his apartment. Einhorn fled to Europe for 23 years.
lastSeen: September 9, 1977, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

sources.title: Murder of Holly Maddux - Wikipedia
Ira Einhorn case - Philadelphia Inquirer
Unicorn Killer - CNN

narrative: On September 9, 1977, thirty-year-old Helen 'Holly' Maddux disappeared from Philadelphia. She had been in a relationship with Ira Einhorn, a charismatic counterculture figure known as the 'Unicorn.' Einhorn told friends Holly had left him to go shopping and never returned.

In March 1979, police searched Einhorn's apartment after following up on neighbors' complaints about a foul odor and a liquid leaking from the ceiling of the apartment below. They found Holly's mummified body in a trunk in Einhorn's closet, packed with newspapers and styrofoam.

Einhorn was charged with murder but fled the country in 1981 while on bail. He lived as a fugitive in Europe for 23 years, residing in Ireland, Sweden, the United Kingdom, and France under various aliases.

He was eventually located in France in 1997 and extradited back to the United States in 2001. Einhorn was convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to life in prison without parole. He died in prison in 2020.

timeline.event: Holly Maddux disappears from Philadelphia.
Holly's body found in a trunk in Einhorn's closet.
Einhorn extradited from France.
Einhorn convicted; sentenced to life.

name: Jeffrey Dahmer Victims
summary: Jeffrey Dahmer murdered 17 men and boys in Milwaukee between 1978 and 1991, engaging in cannibalism and necrophilia. He was convicted and later killed in prison.
lastSeen: Various dates, Milwaukee, Wisconsin

sources.title: Jeffrey Dahmer - Wikipedia
Dahmer case - Milwaukee Journal Sentinel
Monster: The Jeffrey Dahmer Story - Netflix

narrative: Jeffrey Lionel Dahmer murdered 17 men and boys between 1978 and 1991, most of them in his apartment at 924 North 25th Street in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. His victims were predominantly young men of color.

Dahmer's crimes involved drugging victims, strangling them, engaging in necrophilia, dismembering bodies, and in some cases, cannibalism. He preserved body parts as trophies, keeping skulls and other remains in his apartment.

On July 22, 1991, Tracy Edwards escaped from Dahmer's apartment and flagged down police. When officers entered the apartment, they discovered photographs of dismembered bodies and human remains throughout the residence.

Dahmer confessed to all 17 murders. He was found sane and convicted of 15 murders in Wisconsin, receiving 15 consecutive life terms. He was also convicted of one murder in Ohio. On November 28, 1994, Dahmer was beaten to death by fellow inmate Christopher Scarver at the Columbia Correctional Institution.

timeline.event: Dahmer commits his first murder in Ohio.
Tracy Edwards escapes; Dahmer arrested.
Dahmer convicted of 15 murders; sentenced to life.
Dahmer killed in prison by fellow inmate.

name: John Wayne Gacy Victims
summary: Contractor John Wayne Gacy murdered at least 33 young men and boys, burying most under his suburban Chicago home. He was executed in 1994. Several victims remain unidentified.
lastSeen: Various dates, Norwood Park Township, Illinois

sources.title: John Wayne Gacy - Wikipedia
Gacy victims identification - Chicago Tribune
Gacy case - Cook County Sheriff

narrative: John Wayne Gacy, a building contractor and amateur clown entertainer, murdered at least 33 young men and boys between 1972 and 1978 in the Chicago suburb of Norwood Park Township, Illinois.

Gacy lured victims to his home with promises of employment or alcohol, then sexually assaulted and strangled them. He buried 26 of his victims in the crawl space beneath his house and disposed of others in the Des Plaines River.

The investigation began when 15-year-old Robert Piest disappeared after telling his mother he was going to talk to a contractor about a job. That contractor was Gacy. Police surveillance and a search warrant led to the discovery of the mass grave.

Gacy was convicted of 33 murders in 1980 and sentenced to death. He was executed by lethal injection on May 10, 1994. As of 2024, efforts using DNA and genetic genealogy have identified previously unknown victims, but several remain unidentified.

timeline.event: Robert Piest disappears; investigation targets Gacy.
First bodies discovered under Gacy's house.
Gacy convicted of 33 murders.
Gacy executed by lethal injection.

name: Gilgo Beach Victims
summary: At least 10 sets of remains were found along Ocean Parkway near Gilgo Beach, Long Island. Architect Rex Heuermann was arrested in 2023 and charged with multiple murders.
lastSeen: Various dates, Gilgo Beach area, Long Island, New York

sources.title: Gilgo Beach murders - Wikipedia
Rex Heuermann arrest - New York Times
Gilgo Beach investigation - Suffolk County DA

narrative: Beginning in December 2010, police searching for missing woman Shannan Gilbert discovered human remains along a desolate stretch of Ocean Parkway near Gilgo Beach on Long Island's barrier island. Over the following months, at least 10 sets of remains were found in the area.

Most of the identified victims were young women who had advertised as escorts on Craigslist. The discovery revealed that a serial killer had been operating on Long Island, likely for years. The case was hampered by jurisdictional disputes between Suffolk County and other agencies.

A major breakthrough came in July 2023 when Rex Heuermann, a 59-year-old architect from Massapequa Park, Long Island, was arrested at his Manhattan office and charged with multiple murders. The arrest came after investigators linked him through genealogical DNA analysis, cell phone records, and other forensic evidence.
As of 2024, Heuermann has been charged with the murders of six victims and is suspected in others. He has pleaded not guilty. The investigation continues, with the possibility of additional charges.

timeline.event: First remains discovered near Gilgo Beach.
Total of 10 sets of remains found along Ocean Parkway.
Rex Heuermann arrested and charged with multiple murders.

name: Kenneka Jenkins
summary: Nineteen-year-old Kenneka Jenkins was found dead in a walk-in freezer at the Crowne Plaza Chicago O'Hare hotel after a party. Her death was ruled hypothermia. Controversy surrounds the circumstances.
lastSeen: September 8, 2017, Crowne Plaza Chicago O'Hare, Rosemont, Illinois

sources.title: Death of Kenneka Jenkins - Wikipedia
Kenneka Jenkins case - Chicago Tribune
Jenkins family lawsuit - WGN

narrative: On September 8, 2017, nineteen-year-old Kenneka Jenkins attended a party on the ninth floor of the Crowne Plaza Chicago O'Hare hotel in Rosemont, Illinois. During the party, she became heavily intoxicated. Her friends later reported that she wandered away from the gathering.

When Jenkins didn't return, her mother Teresa Martin went to the hotel and demanded that staff search for her daughter. After initially being turned away, hotel staff and police eventually searched the building and found Kenneka's body in a walk-in freezer in the hotel's kitchen area on September 10.

Security camera footage showed Kenneka stumbling through the hotel's hallways and entering the kitchen area alone. The Cook County Medical Examiner ruled her death accidental, caused by hypothermia with ethanol intoxication as a contributing factor.

The case sparked significant controversy and social media attention. Jenkins's family disputed the finding and filed a wrongful death lawsuit against the hotel, arguing that security failures allowed an intoxicated teenager to access a dangerous kitchen area.

timeline.event: Kenneka Jenkins attends party at Crowne Plaza hotel.
Her body found in a walk-in freezer.
Death ruled accidental hypothermia.

name: Keddie Murders
summary: Three people were bludgeoned and stabbed in cabin 28 at the Keddie Resort in rural Northern California. A fourth victim, a 12-year-old girl, was also murdered. The case has never been solved.
lastSeen: April 11, 1981, Cabin 28, Keddie Resort, Plumas County, California

sources.title: Keddie murders - Wikipedia
Keddie murders case - Sacramento Bee
Plumas County cold case

narrative: On April 12, 1981, the bodies of Glenna Sharp (36), her son John (15), and his friend Dana Wingate (17) were discovered in cabin 28 at the Keddie Resort in rural Plumas County, California. They had been bound, bludgeoned with a hammer, and stabbed with a steak knife and a butter knife.

Glenna's daughter Tina Sharp, 12, was missing from the scene. Two other children who had been sleeping in the cabin were unharmed. Tina's skull was found three years later in a neighboring county, confirming she had also been murdered.

Despite extensive investigation, the case went cold. In 2016, the Plumas County Sheriff's Office announced a renewed investigation. DNA evidence was tested using modern techniques, and two suspects were identified: Martin Smartt and John 'Bo' Boubede, both of whom had been staying in a neighboring cabin. Both men had died before the renewed investigation.
Cabin 28 was demolished in 2004. The case remains one of California's most notorious unsolved mass murders.

timeline.event: Three bodies found in cabin 28; Tina Sharp missing.
Tina Sharp's skull found in neighboring county.
Case reopened; suspects identified but both deceased.

name: Robert Durst Victims
summary: Real estate heir Robert Durst was connected to three killings spanning decades. He was convicted of murdering Susan Berman and suspected in the disappearance of his wife Kathie.
lastSeen: Various dates and locations

sources.title: Robert Durst - Wikipedia
The Jinx - HBO
Durst conviction - New York Times

narrative: Robert Durst, heir to a New York real estate empire, was connected to three separate killings. His first wife, Kathleen McCormack Durst, vanished in 1982 and has never been found. Durst was long suspected but never charged in her disappearance.

In December 2000, Durst's close friend Susan Berman was found shot execution-style in her Benedict Canyon home in Los Angeles. Berman had reportedly been about to speak to investigators about Kathie Durst's disappearance.

While awaiting trial for Berman's murder, Durst fled to Galveston, Texas, where he disguised himself as a mute woman and rented a room. In September 2001, his neighbor Morris Black was found dismembered in Galveston Bay. Durst was acquitted of murder but convicted of evidence tampering for dismembering the body.

In the 2015 HBO documentary 'The Jinx,' Durst appeared to confess on a hot microphone, saying 'What the hell did I do? Killed them all, of course.' He was arrested for Susan Berman's murder and convicted in 2021. Durst died in prison in January 2022.

timeline.event: Kathleen Durst disappears; never found.
Susan Berman found murdered in Los Angeles.
Morris Black's dismembered remains found in Galveston Bay.
Durst convicted of murdering Susan Berman.
Durst dies in prison.

name: Teresa Halbach (Making a Murderer)
summary: Photographer Teresa Halbach was murdered in Manitowoc County, Wisconsin. Steven Avery and his nephew Brendan Dassey were convicted. The case was featured in Netflix's 'Making a Murderer.'
lastSeen: October 31, 2005, Avery Auto Salvage, Manitowoc County, Wisconsin

sources.title: Murder of Teresa Halbach - Wikipedia
Making a Murderer - Netflix
Steven Avery case - Milwaukee Journal Sentinel

narrative: On October 31, 2005, twenty-five-year-old freelance photographer Teresa Halbach visited the Avery Auto Salvage yard in Manitowoc County, Wisconsin, to photograph a vehicle for Auto Trader magazine. She was never seen again.

Teresa's vehicle was found on the Avery property on November 5. Her remains were later found in a burn pit behind Steven Avery's trailer, and her car key was found in his bedroom. Avery, who had recently been exonerated after spending 18 years in prison for a wrongful sexual assault conviction, was charged with her murder.

Avery's 16-year-old nephew Brendan Dassey provided a confession implicating both himself and Avery, though Dassey later recanted, saying investigators had coerced his statements. Both were convicted: Avery of first-degree intentional homicide, and Dassey of first-degree intentional homicide, mutilation of a corpse, and second-degree sexual assault.

The 2015 Netflix documentary 'Making a Murderer' raised questions about the fairness of the investigation and trial, generating massive public debate about potential evidence planting and Dassey's coerced confession. Appeals have been ongoing but both men remain in prison.

timeline.event: Teresa Halbach visits Avery property and disappears.
Her vehicle found on Avery property.
Steven Avery convicted; sentenced to life without parole.
Brendan Dassey convicted; sentenced to life with parole eligibility in 2048.

name: Sarah Stern
summary: Nineteen-year-old Sarah Stern was murdered by childhood friend Liam McAtasney for inheritance money. Her body was thrown off a bridge. McAtasney was convicted after being secretly recorded confessing.
lastSeen: December 2, 2016, her home in Neptune City, New Jersey

sources.title: Murder of Sarah Stern - Wikipedia
Liam McAtasney trial - Asbury Park Press
Sarah Stern case - NBC New York

narrative: On December 2, 2016, nineteen-year-old Sarah Stern disappeared from Neptune City, New Jersey. Her car was found abandoned on the Route 35 bridge over the Shark River, initially suggesting suicide.

The investigation took a turn when authorities received information from Anthony Curry, a friend of Liam McAtasney, who had been Sarah's childhood friend. Curry had secretly recorded McAtasney confessing in graphic detail to strangling Sarah in her home and then, with the help of Preston Taylor, throwing her body off the bridge into the Shark River.

McAtasney's motive was money—Sarah had recently received a cash inheritance from her late mother, and McAtasney planned to steal it. The recording captured McAtasney describing the murder in chilling detail.

McAtasney was convicted of first-degree murder, robbery, and other charges in 2019 and sentenced to life in prison without parole plus additional years. Taylor pleaded guilty to robbery, desecration of human remains, and other charges and received an 18-year sentence. Sarah's body was never recovered from the river.

timeline.event: Sarah Stern murdered by Liam McAtasney.
McAtasney and Taylor arrested.
McAtasney convicted; sentenced to life without parole.

name: Tylee Ryan & JJ Vallow
summary: Siblings Tylee Ryan and JJ Vallow were murdered by their mother Lori Vallow Daybell and her husband Chad Daybell. The case involved doomsday beliefs and multiple other deaths.
lastSeen: September 2019, Rexburg, Idaho

sources.title: Murders of Tylee Ryan and JJ Vallow - Wikipedia
Lori Vallow Daybell trial - East Idaho News
Daybell case - CNN

narrative: In September 2019, sixteen-year-old Tylee Ryan and seven-year-old Joshua 'JJ' Vallow disappeared from Rexburg, Idaho. Their mother, Lori Vallow, and her new husband, Chad Daybell, told conflicting stories about the children's whereabouts.

Extended family members raised the alarm when they could not contact the children. When police conducted a welfare check in November 2019, Lori and Chad had fled Idaho. They were eventually located in Hawaii in January 2020.

On June 9, 2020, investigators found the children's remains on Chad Daybell's property. Tylee's remains had been burned, and JJ's body was wrapped in plastic and duct tape. The case revealed a web of deaths connected to the couple, including Lori's previous husband Charles Vallow and Chad's previous wife Tammy Daybell.

Both were convicted of multiple counts of murder. Chad Daybell was sentenced to death, and Lori Vallow Daybell was sentenced to life without parole. The case involved extreme religious beliefs, with the couple allegedly believing certain people were 'dark' spirits who needed to be eliminated.

name: Macin Smith
summary: Seventeen-year-old Macin Smith left his St. George, Utah home on the first day of school and vanished. Surveillance showed him walking into the desert. He has never been found.
lastSeen: September 1, 2015, walking along Bluff Street, St. George, Utah

sources.title: Disappearance of Macin Smith - Wikipedia
Macin Smith case - KSL
FindMacinSmith.com

narrative: On September 1, 2015, seventeen-year-old Macin Smith left his family's home in St. George, Utah, on what was supposed to be his first day of school at Desert Hills High School. He never arrived at school.

Surveillance cameras captured Macin walking along Bluff Street in St. George and eventually heading into the desert toward the Red Cliffs area. His cell phone was later found at a construction site. Despite extensive ground searches and aerial sweeps of the surrounding desert terrain, no trace of Macin was found.
The investigation revealed that Macin had been dealing with the effects of his parents' divorce and a recent move. His family has said he showed no signs of suicidal ideation.
Macin's family has maintained an active search, including hiring private investigators and organizing volunteer search parties in the rugged red rock terrain around St. George.

name: Joey Lynn Offutt
summary: Joey Lynn Offutt vanished from her rural Pennsylvania home, leaving behind four young children. In 2023, her boyfriend was charged with her murder after her remains were found.
lastSeen: July 12, 2007, her home near Sykesville, Jefferson County, Pennsylvania

sources.title: Disappearance of Joey Lynn Offutt - Wikipedia
Joey Lynn Offutt case - WTAJ
PA cold case solved - AP News

narrative: On July 12, 2007, thirty-year-old Joey Lynn Offutt disappeared from her home near Sykesville in rural Jefferson County, Pennsylvania. Her four young children were left in the home alone. Her boyfriend, James Sheehan, reported her missing.
The investigation stalled for years. Sheehan maintained that Joey Lynn had left voluntarily, but her family disputed this, noting she would never have abandoned her children.

In 2023, a renewed investigation led by Pennsylvania State Police resulted in the discovery of Joey Lynn's remains on property connected to Sheehan. He was arrested and charged with criminal homicide.
The case was one of many cold cases in rural Pennsylvania that benefited from advances in forensic technology and renewed investigative efforts.

name: Madeline Kingsbury
summary: Twenty-six-year-old Madeline Kingsbury vanished after being dropped off by her ex-boyfriend Adam Fravel in Winona, Minnesota. Fravel was convicted of her murder.
lastSeen: March 31, 2023, Winona, Minnesota

narrative: On March 31, 2023, twenty-six-year-old Madeline Kingsbury disappeared in Winona, Minnesota. Her ex-boyfriend and father of her two children, Adam Fravel, told police he had dropped her off at their shared home after taking the children to daycare. She was never seen again.
Volunteers and law enforcement conducted extensive searches of the Winona area. On June 7, 2023, Madeline's body was found in a rural area of Fillmore County, about 30 miles from Winona.

Fravel was arrested and charged with second-degree murder. The investigation revealed a history of domestic abuse and controlling behavior. Evidence including Fravel's internet searches and cell phone data contradicted his account.
Fravel was convicted of first-degree and second-degree murder in 2024 and sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole.

name: Etan Patz
summary: Six-year-old Etan Patz vanished while walking to his school bus stop in SoHo, Manhattan. His case helped launch the missing children movement. Pedro Hernandez was convicted in 2017.
lastSeen: May 25, 1979, West Broadway, SoHo, Manhattan, New York

sources.title: Disappearance of Etan Patz - Wikipedia
Etan Patz case - New York Times
Pedro Hernandez conviction - NBC New York

narrative: On May 25, 1979, six-year-old Etan Patz left his SoHo apartment in Lower Manhattan to walk two blocks to his school bus stop—the first time he was allowed to walk alone. He never arrived at the bus stop and was never seen again.

The case became one of the most famous missing child cases in American history. Etan was one of the first missing children to appear on milk cartons. The date of his disappearance, May 25, was designated National Missing Children's Day by President Reagan in 1983.
For decades, the case remained unsolved. Prime suspect Jose Antonio Ramos, a convicted pedophile linked to Etan's babysitter, was arrested for other crimes but never charged in Etan's case.

In 2012, Pedro Hernandez, a former bodega worker who had operated a store near the bus stop, confessed to luring Etan into the store with the promise of a soda and then strangling him. His first trial ended in a hung jury in 2015. He was convicted of murder in a second trial in 2017 and sentenced to 25 years to life.

name: Mary Boyle
summary: Six-year-old Mary Boyle vanished while walking across bogland to visit her uncle's house in County Donegal, Ireland. She is Ireland's longest-running missing child case.
lastSeen: March 18, 1977, Cashelard, near Ballyshannon, County Donegal, Ireland

sources.title: Disappearance of Mary Boyle - Wikipedia
Mary Boyle case - Irish Times
Mary Boyle documentary - RTÉ

narrative: On March 18, 1977, six-year-old Mary Boyle was visiting her grandparents' home in Cashelard, a remote area near Ballyshannon in County Donegal, Ireland. She followed her uncle across a field toward a neighbor's house. Her uncle turned back for a moment, and when he looked again, Mary was gone.

An immediate search of the surrounding bogland, fields, and lakes was conducted. The area was rugged and sparsely populated, with bogs that could potentially conceal a body. Despite extensive searches, no trace of Mary was ever found.

The case has been one of the most controversial cold cases in Irish history. Mary's twin sister Ann and other family members have publicly accused a family member of involvement in Mary's disappearance, creating a deep rift within the family.
Multiple investigations and reviews by An Garda Síochána have failed to result in charges. The case remains Ireland's longest-running missing child case.

timeline.event: Mary Boyle vanishes while walking across bogland in County Donegal.
